title: Power Pages: self-service site ownership transfer in the Power Platform admin center
summary: Hold: the controls table and several standalone prerequisite statements require website app ownership without the documented exception for managed identity sites. The navigation, audit command and roadmap details are supported; minor corrections should also acknowledge conflicting ownership documentation and checklist controls missing from the table.

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-10-22T23:45:49.
An authorised user can transfer a Power Pages site to another user in the organisation.
claims.quote: Transfer ownership of a Power Pages site when responsibility for managing the site moves to another user in your organization.

claims.claim: The transfer does not require a support request.
claims.quote: Existing site owners and global administrators can assign ownership to another valid user within the tenant without requiring manual intervention from support.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The selected user becomes the site's primary owner when the transfer finishes.
claims.quote: When the transfer finishes, the selected user becomes the primary owner of the site. Verify that the new owner can access and manage the site.
claims.fix: Keep this statement, but add: 'The roles page still says website ownership remains with the creator and cannot be transferred or changed, whereas the transfer page documents a new primary owner.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/admin/admin-roles#website-owner alongside the transfer page; both pages were read and disagree on this point.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; What's changing; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The transfer path is Power Platform admin center > Manage > Power Pages > site > Site Details > Edit > Owner.
claims.quote: In the left navigation pane, select Manage, and then select Power Pages. Select the Power Pages site that you want to update. On the Site Details page, select Edit. In the Owner field, remove the current owner and search for the new owner.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: No transfer API or pac command is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages transfer ownership API pac pages PowerShell Set-AdminPowerAppPortalOwner tenant setting notification. Opened transfer-ownership, admin-api, Power Platform Websites REST operations and pac pages references; no transfer operation.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing; Scope; rendered table
claims.claim: Website app ownership is a prerequisite for initiating a transfer, without an exception in these standalone statements.
claims.quote: Websites on Power Platform managed identity model don't need web app ownership as a prerequisite for initiating transfer.
claims.fix: In controls[0].note and its rendered copy, and in the unqualified prerequisite statements in Risk assessment, Cost and licensing and Scope, qualify website app ownership with: 'Website app ownership is required except for sites using the Power Platform managed identity model.' Retain the three admin-role alternatives and the new-owner requirements. The exception already stated in What's changing and Governance controls must also qualify the table and these standalone statements.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist's role-assignment inventory and environment auditing-setup controls are represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Confirm who holds ... roles' and 'Check that Microsoft Purview auditing is configured for the production environments'. Table rows: 'Transferring ownership of a Power Pages site' and 'Audit trail of site ownership transfers'.
claims.fix: The first Before rollout bullet (taking stock of directly assigned administrator roles) and the second (checking production-environment auditing configuration) have no corresponding control rows; the audit row only searches logs. Remove these checklist instructions rather than adding unverified control rows.

claims.claim: Ownership does not change until an authorised user initiates and confirms a transfer.
claims.quote: Select the new owner, and then select Save. Review the confirmation message, and then select Transfer. When the transfer finishes, the selected user becomes the primary owner of the site.
